p.seg: The people of Qín 秦 attacked Jìn 晉.
9.12 *Xiāng Gōng* (Duke Xiang) Year 12
9.12.1 In the spring, the third month of the king's year twelve,
the people of Jǔ 莒 attacked my eastern border and
besieged Tái 邰.
Attacking a state, it is not mentioned that they besieged a town,
to emphasize the gravity of the attack.
If a town is captured, besieging it is not recorded,
as it is considered not worth mentioning.
9.12.2 Jìsūn Sù 季孫宿 led the army to rescue Tái 邰,
and subsequently entered Yùn 鄆.
"Subsequently" means a successive event,
Received orders and rescued Tái;
did not receive orders and entered Yùn,
disliking Jìsūn Sù.
9.12.3 In summer,
the Marquis of Jìn sent Shì Fáng to come for a formal visit.
9.12.4 In the ninth month, autumn,
Wú Zǐ Chéng died.
9.12.5 In winter,
Chǔ Gōngzǐ Zhēn led an army to invade Sòng.
9.12.6 Duke (Xiāng Gōng) went to Jìn.
9.13 *Xiāng Gōng, Year 13*
9.13.1 In the spring of the thirteenth year,
the Duke returned from Jìn.
Yǐn Gōng
1.1 *Yǐn Gōng Yuánnián*
1.1.1 "The first year, spring, the king's first month." Even if there is nothing to record,
the first month must be mentioned;
this is to be careful about beginnings.
Why does the Duke not mention his accession?
It is to fulfill Duke Chéng's intention.
How is it fulfilled?
It speaks of the ruler not taking [the throne] to become Duke.
Why does the ruler not take [the throne] to become Duke?
It is because he intends to yield to Huán.
Is this Huán's right?
I say
it is not right.
*Chūnqiū* fulfills the beauty of people,
and does not fulfill the evil of people.
Yǐn's unrighteousness is fulfilled;
why?
It is to detest Huán.
Why is Huán detested?
If Yǐn intends to yield and Huán slays him,
then Huán is evil.
If Huán slays and Yǐn yields,
then Yǐn is good.
If it is good, how can it be considered improper?
Why is that?
*Chūnqiū* (Spring and Autumn Annals) values righteousness and not kindness,
believes in the correct way and not in evil.
A filial son praises his father's good deeds,
but does not praise his father's bad deeds.
The former ruler's desire to form an alliance with [Qí Huán] 桓,
was not correct,
but evil.
However,
having already overcome his evil intentions and allied with [Yǐn] 隱,
having already discovered the former ruler's evil ambitions,
but then proceeded to ally with [Qí Huán] 桓,
this would be completing his father's evil.
Brothers
are a natural bond;
as a son, one receives from one's father;
as a feudal lord, one receives from one's ruler.
Having already abandoned the natural bond
and forgotten ruler and father,
to pursue petty kindness,
this is called a petty path.
As for [Yǐn] 隱,
one could say he disregarded a state of a thousand chariots,
but to have truly walked the path
he has not yet done.
1.1.2 In the third month,
Duke (Yǐn) and Yífù of Zhū made an alliance at Mèi.
What does "jí" (及, and) mean?
It is used to internally record the event.
Yí,
is his courtesy name.
Fù,
is like "tutor,"
a respectful term for a man.
Why is he not referred to as the Viscount of Zhū?
Why?
Zhū in ancient times was insignificant,
and had not yet received a title from the Zhou Dynasty.
It does not mention the day,
implying the alliance would be broken.
Mèi,
is a place name.
1.1.3 In summer,
in the fifth month,
Lord Zhèng overcame Duàn at Yān.
What does "kè" (克, overcome) mean?
It means "able."
Able to do what?
Able to kill.
Why is "kill" not used?
Because it shows that Duàn had followers.
Duàn,
was the younger brother of Lord Zhèng,
How do we know that he was a younger brother?
He killed the heir apparent, his own younger brother, to become the ruler.
Because he became the ruler after killing his younger brother,
we know that he was a younger brother.
Duàn,
was a younger brother,
but he was not called younger brother.
He was a son of a duke,
but he was not called a son of a duke.
This is to degrade him.
Duàn lost the proper way of a younger brother.
By demeaning Duàn, we are condemning Zhèng Bó even more.
Why condemn Zhèng Bó so much?
We condemn Zhèng Bó's harboring of intentions and accumulating plans
until it resulted in murder.
Even though Yān
was far away,
it was still said that it was like taking him from his mother's arms and killing him,
condemning it greatly.
Then what should the one who is Zhèng Bó have done?
Slowly pursue the fleeing rebel;
this is the way of being close to one's relatives.
1.1.4 In the autumn,
in the seventh month,
the Heavenly King sent Zǎi Xuǎn to return the gifts for the funeral of Huì Gōng's Zhòngzǐ.
The mother is named after her son.
Who was Zhòngzǐ?
The mother of Duke Huì (Huì Gōng)
was a concubine of Duke Xiào (Xiào Gōng).
According to ritual,
it is permissible to present funerary gifts (賵, pèng) to someone's mother,
but not to someone's concubine.
A gentleman would decline such gifts because they are inappropriate,
and moreover, to record
such a trivial matter is unwarranted.
What are funerary gifts (賵, pèng)?
Horses and chariots are called 賵 (pèng),
garments and shrouds are called 襚 (suì),
cowrie shells and jades are called 含 (hán),
and money and goods are called 賻 (fù).
1.1.5 In the ninth month,
they made an alliance with the people of Sòng (宋) at Sù (宿).
What does "及 (jí)" [used in the phrase "及宋人", "and the people of Sòng"] mean?
It signifies subordination of the inner party [the state of Lǔ].
The people of Sòng (宋)
signify subordination of the outer party.
An alliance of subordinates is not recorded with a specific date.
Sù (宿)
is the name of a town.
1.1.6 In the winter,
the twelfth month,
the Earl of Jì (祭伯) came.
"Came" means
To come to court.
Why is it not called "to court"?
The various lords within the realm
cannot meet with other lords without the Son of Heaven's command.
They cannot conduct their own foreign affairs.
Therefore, it is not considered "to court."
Gifts of bows and arrows
do not leave the boundary field,
and bundles of dried meat
do not go beyond the center of the boundary.
One must not have divided loyalties to the supreme ruler.
1.1.7 Gōngzǐ Yì Shī died.
For a grand master to be recorded as dying "on a day"
is proper;
not recorded as dying "on a day"
is bad.
1.2 Yǐn Gōng, Year 2
1.2.1 In the second year
of spring,
the Duke met with the Róng at Qián.
To meet
means that the outside party is in charge.
The wise deliberate,
the righteous act,
The benevolent man guards;
having these three things,
then he can go to a meeting.
(He) met with the Róng,
(and) Duke Wēi.
1.2.2 In summer,
in the fifth month,
the people of Jǔ entered Xiàng.
"Entered" means
the inside did not accept (them);
Xiàng
was our city.
1.2.3 Wú Gāi led an army to enter Jí.
"Entered" means
the inside did not accept (them);
Jí
was a state.
If one is intent on entering others,
others will also enter him.
Not mentioning the clan name
is because (they) destroyed (a state of) the same surname,
a debasement.
1.2.4 In autumn, on the *gēng chén* day of the eighth month,
the Duke made an alliance with the Róng at Táng.
1.2.5 In the ninth month,
Jǐ Lǚxū (紀履緰) came to escort his daughter.
To escort a daughter,
who is a close relative,
using a senior minister
is improper.
Regarding the use of the state name,
it is because he came to establish relations with us,
therefore the *jūnzǐ* advances it.
1.2.6 In the winter,
in the tenth month,
Bó Jī (伯姬) went to Jì (紀) in marriage.
According to ritual,
women call marriage "going" (歸),
and returning is called "coming back" (來歸),
following others.
A woman at home
is governed by her father,
after marriage
she is governed by her husband,
when the husband dies,
she follows the eldest son.
A woman does not act independently,
she must have someone to follow.
Bó Jī (伯姬) went to Jì (紀) in marriage,
how can this be explained as a matter of independent action?
It is said:
It was not a solitary action.
My Bó Jī 伯姬 married into Jǐ 紀,
therefore it is recorded.
Why is there no mention of an envoy?
The way of defiance is subtle,
nothing worthy of mention.
1.2.7 Jǐ Zǐbó 紀子伯 and Jǔ Zǐ 莒子 formed an alliance in Mì 密.
Some say: Jǐ Zǐbó 紀子伯 and Jǔ Zǐ 莒子 both participated in the alliance,
some say they were of the same age and rank,
therefore Jǐ Zǐ 紀子 is placed before with the title Bó 伯.
1.2.8 In the twelfth month,
on Yǐmǎo 乙卯,
Fūrén Zǐ Shì 夫人子氏 died.
When a Fūrén 夫人 dies,
she is not buried in a separate plot.
A Fūrén 夫人,
is the wife of Yǐn 隱.
Her death is recorded but not her burial,
because the duty of a Fūrén 夫人,
is to follow her lord.
1.2.9 The people of Zhèng 鄭 attacked Wèi 衛.
1.3 *The Third Year of Duke Yǐn 隱*
1.3.1 In the third year,
spring,
In the second month,
on the day jǐsì,
there was a solar eclipse.
The text says "day" and does not say "new moon,"
the eclipse
occurred on the dark day.
Why is it said that "on that day, there was an eclipse?"
What is the reason for "[on that day] there was an eclipse"?
"Tǔ" refers to the outer edge,
"shí" refers to the inner edge.
The absence of seeing its edges
means "there was an eclipse."
"Yǒu" and "nèi" are internal terms,
"huò" is an external term.
"Yǒu shí zhī zhě" [there was an eclipse]
means it is inside the sun.
Why does it not say "shí zhī" [eclipse]?
Knowing what cannot be known
is wisdom.
1.3.2 In the third month,
on the day gēngxū,
the Heavenly King died.
High is called "bēng",
thick is called "bēng",
honorable is called "bēng",
the death of the Son of Heaven
is called "bēng" because of his honor.
What is meant by "collapse"?
It is because he was above the people,
therefore he "collapsed."
Why is his name not mentioned?
Because he was the *tàishàng* (太上, supreme ruler),
therefore his name is not mentioned.
1.3.3 In the summer,
in the fourth month,
on the *xīnmǎo* (辛卯) day,
Yǐnshì (尹氏) died.
What was Yǐnshì?
He was a grand master of the Son of Heaven.
Outer grand masters are not recorded as having died,
why is this one recorded as having died?
Because at the time of the Son of Heaven's collapse, he was the master representing Lǔ,
therefore it is recorded that he died in seclusion.
1.3.4 In the autumn,
a son of the Wǔshì (武氏) came to request a burial gift.
What was this son of the Wǔshì?
He was a grand master of the Son of Heaven.
He was a grand master of the Son of Heaven;
why is he referred to as "son of the Wǔshì"?
Because the mourning period had not yet concluded,
the orphan had not yet received a title,
he had not received a title, yet was sent,
it was not proper.
Why is it not mentioned that someone was sent?
Because there was no ruler.
To send gifts to the dead is called "fèng" (賵).
To send gifts to the living is called "fù" (賻).
To say "guī zhī zhě" (曰歸之者, to return it)
is proper ("zhèng" 正).
To seek it ("qiú zhī zhě" 求之者)
is improper ("fēi zhèng" 非正).
Although Zhōu (周) did not seek it,
Lǔ (魯) could not not return it;
although Lǔ (魯) did not return it,
Zhōu (周) could not seek it.
The phrase "to seek it" ("qiú zhī wèi yán" 求之為言)
implies that whether one will
get it or not is unknown.
They mutually criticized this.
1.3.5 In the eighth month,
on the day gēng-chén (庚辰),
Duke Hé (和) of Sòng (宋) died.
To record the day of death of the various lords
is proper.
1.3.6 In winter,
in the twelfth month,
the Marquis of Qí (齊) and the Count of Zhèng (鄭) made a covenant at Shímén (石門).
1.3.7 On guǐ-wèi (癸未) day,
Buried Sòng Mù Gōng.
A burial on a "day"
but in times of turmoil, burial was not possible.
1.4 *Yǐn Gōng, Year 4*
1.4.1 Fourth Year
In the spring, the second month of the king's reign,
the people of Jǔ attacked Qǐ,
and took Móu and Lóu.
The *Commentary* says:
"To say 'attacked' and 'took'
is what is detested."
"It was from this point that the feudal lords began to attack each other
and seize territory, so [the text] carefully records it."
1.4.2 On the day wù-shēn,
Wèi Zhù Xū assassinated his lord, Wán.
When a grandee assassinates his lord
and the state surname is used [to designate the assassin],
it indicates suspicion,
as the assassin replaced him.
1.4.3 In summer,
the Duke and the Duke of Sòng met at Qīng.
"Met with"
內為志焉爾. Internally, it was recorded as their intention.
遇者、 "Yù zhě" (encounter) refers to,
志相得也. the mutual agreement of their intentions.
1.4.4 Sòng gōng, Chén hóu, Cài rén, Wèi rén fá Zhèng. Duke Sòng, Marquis Chén, the people of Cài, and the people of Wèi attacked Zhèng.
1.4.5 Qiū, In autumn,
Huī shuài shī huì Sòng gōng, Chén hóu, Cài rén, Wèi rén fá Zhèng. Huī led the army and joined Duke Sòng, Marquis Chén, the people of Cài, and the people of Wèi to attack Zhèng.
Huī zhě hé yě? Who is Huī?
Gōngzǐ Huī yě. He is Gōngzǐ Huī.
Qí bù chēng gōngzǐ hé yě? Why is he not referred to as "Gōngzǐ"?
Biǎn zhī yě. It is a demotion of him.
Hé wéi biǎn zhī yě? Why is he demoted?
Yǔ yú shì gōng, Because he participated in the assassination of the duke,
gù biǎn zhī yě. therefore he is demoted.
1.4.6 Jiǔ yuè, In the ninth month,
Wèi rén shā Zhù Xū yú Pú. The people of Wèi killed Zhù Xū in Pú.
Chēng rén yǐ shā, The use of "rén" (people) with "shā" (kill) indicates
shā yǒu zuì yě. that the killing was of someone who was guilty.
Zhù Xū zhī qiè, Zhù Xū's (behavior) of enticement (suggests)
shī xián yě. a failure to avoid suspicion.
Qí yuè, The specifying of the month indicates
jǐn zhī yě. carefulness in recording it.
Yú Pú zhě, The phrase "yú Pú" (in Pú)
jī shī zéi yě. criticizes the loss of the thief (i.e., Zhù Xū).
1.4.7 Dōng, In winter,
In the twelfth month,
the people of Wèi installed Jìn.
"The people of Wèi"
is a collective expression;
"installed" means one who should not have been installed.
The name of Jìn is an evil.
Why does it refer to "the people" installing him?
It is because he gained the support of the people.
If he gained the support of the people, then he is virtuous,
so why does it say he should not have been installed?
The principle of the *Chūnqiū*
is to side with legitimacy rather than virtue among the feudal lords.
1.5 *Yǐn Gōng*, Year 5
1.5.1 Year 5
In spring,
the Duke watched the fish at Táng.
The *Commentary* says:
Regular matters are called "shì" (視),
extraordinary matters are called "guān" (觀).
According to ritual,
those of high status do not personally attend to minor matters,
and those of low status do not take credit for great achievements.
Fish
are the affair of the lowly,
yet the Duke watched them,
which is not proper.
1.5.2 In the fourth month of summer,
the funeral of Duke Huán of Wèi took place.
The burial in the month
was the established practice.
1.5.3 In the autumn,
the army of Wèi entered Chéng.
"Entered" means
they were not received internally.
Chéng
was a state,
calling a large army from a subordinate state "army."
1.5.4 In the ninth month,
the palace for Zhòngzǐ was completed.
What does "completed" mean?
"Completed" means
it was finished,
its completion signifies that she became the First Lady.
According to ritual,
when a son of a concubine becomes the ruler,
he builds a palace for his mother
and has a son of the previous ruler preside over her sacrifices.
The sacrifices continue with the son
and cease with the grandson.
Zhòngzǐ was
the mother of Duke Huì,
To conceal a grandson and then cultivate him is not true concealment.
fēi yǐn yě.
The first offering (involved) six plumes.
"First"
means "beginning".
Master Gǔliáng said:
"When performing the *xià* dance,
the Son of Heaven used eight rows of dancers,
the Dukes used six rows,
and the lords used four rows.
The first offering (involved) six plumes,
thus, it began the usurpation of ritual music."
Master Shī said:
"When performing the *xià* dance,
from the Son of Heaven to the lords,
all used eight rows of dancers,
the first offering (involved) six plumes,
thus, it began the abuse of ritual music."
1.5.5 The people of Zhū and the people of Zhèng attacked Sòng.
1.5.6 Caterpillars (appeared). This is an insect disaster,
when severe, it is by the month,
when not severe, it is by the season.
1.5.7 In winter,
in the twelfth month,
on *xīnsì* day,
Gōngzǐ Kōu 公子罿 died.
(The *Chūnqiū*) conceals (his death), not mentioning the conferring of rank upon a senior minister.
Why does it say "Gōngzǐ Kōu 公子罿"?
He was a senior minister of the former lord.
1.5.8 The people of Sòng 宋 attacked Zhèng 鄭 and
besieged Chánggé 長葛.
Attacking a state does not warrant mentioning the besieging of a town.
Why does it say "besieged" here?
It was prolonged.
An attack should not exceed its season,
a battle should not pursue those who flee,
and executions should not fill up the subjugated.
Enclosing people,
and driving away cattle and horses
is called "encroachment."
Cutting down trees and destroying palaces and houses
is called "attacking."
1.6 *Yǐn Gōng* 隱公, Year Six
1.6.1 In the sixth year,
in spring,
the people of Zhèng 鄭 came to deliver a peace treaty.
"Deliver" (輸 *shū*) means
to fall or decline.
The meaning of "peace" (平 *píng*)
It is achieved through principle.
Those who come to submit peacefully
are not to be attacked.
1.6.2 In the summer,
in the fifth month,
on the day of Xīnyǒu,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí
and made a covenant at Ài.
1.6.3 In the autumn,
in the seventh month.
1.6.4 In the winter,
the people of Sòng seized Chánggé.
External seizures of towns are not recorded,
so why is this one recorded?
It was long-standing.
1.7 *The Seventh Year of Duke Yǐn*
1.7.1 In the seventh year,
in the spring,
in the third month of the King,
Shū Jī was sent back to Jǐ.
Why is it not stated that she was returned forcibly?
The way of forced return is subtle,
not worth mentioning.
1.7.2 The Marquis of Téng died.
The Marquis of Téng had no name.
In youth, he was called the heir apparent (shìzǐ);
when he grew up, he was called the lord (jūn).
This is the way of the Dí.
What is incorrect is his name.
1.7.3 In summer,
the city of Zhōngqiū was walled.
Wall-building
is done to protect the people.
If the populace increases and the city is small,
then the city is expanded,
and there is no limit to expanding the city.
All records of wall-building
are criticisms.
1.7.4 The Marquis of Qí sent his younger brother Nián to come and pay a formal visit.
Among the nobles,
brothers cannot communicate through intermediaries.
The reference to "his younger brother"
is because he came to connect with us.
He is referred to by his noble title.
1.7.5 In autumn,
the Duke attacked Zhū.
the King of Heaven sent Fán Bó to come and pay a formal visit.
The Róng attacked Fán Bó at Chǔqiū and returned with him.
What is Fán Bó's status?
He is a senior official of the Son of Heaven.
Why does the text use "attack" (伐) when referring to a state,
and also use "attack" (伐) when referring to a single person?
What is the reason?
It is to emphasize the importance of the Son of Heaven's command.
Róng refers to
Wèi.
"Róng Wèi" is used
because they attacked the Son of Heaven's envoy,
so they are downgraded and referred to as Róng.
Chǔqiū is
a city of Wèi.
"Returned with him"
is still better than "captured him."
1.8 *Yǐn Gōng*, Year 8
1.8.1 Eighth Year
In spring,
Sòng Gōng and Wèi Hóu met at Chuí.
To meet without prior arrangement is called "encounter" (遇).
"Encounter" means
the intentions are in accord.
1.8.2 In the third month,
Zhèng Bó sent Yuān to return Bǐng.
Naming him Yuān
The reason for criticizing Zhèng Bó 鄭伯 (Earl of Zheng)
is to express disapproval of his involvement with the land (of Bǐng 邴).
1.8.3 On the day Gēngyín 庚寅,
we entered Bǐng 邴.
"Entering" means
that the people inside did not accept us.
The use of "day" to describe the entry
expresses disapproval of the entry.
Bǐng 邴 was
a city where the Earl of Zhèng 鄭伯 received his mandate from the Son of Heaven
and performed sacrifices to Mount Tài 泰山.
1.8.4 In summer,
the sixth month,
on the day Jǐhài 己亥,
the Marquis Kǎofù 考父 of Cài 蔡 died.
The use of "day" for the death of a feudal lord
is proper.
1.8.5 On the day Xīnhài 辛亥,
the Viscount of Sù 宿 died.
Sù 宿
was a small state
and had not yet joined the alliance,
therefore he is referred to as "Viscount" upon his death.
1.8.6 In autumn,
Seventh month,
on the day of Gēngwǔ,
For outer covenants, a date is not specified.
Why is a date specified for this one?
This was the beginning of the feudal lords participating in covenants,
Sòng Gōng, Qí Hóu, and Wèi Hóu made a covenant at Wǎwū.
therefore it was done carefully and a date was specified.
Solemn pronouncements and oaths do not reach back to the Five Emperors,
covenants and curses do not reach back to the Three Kings,
and the exchange of hostages does not reach back to the Two Hegemons.
1.8.7 In the eighth month,
the XUān Gōng of Cài was buried.
Burying within the month
is customary.
1.8.8 In the ninth month,
on the day of Xīnmǎo,
the Duke and the people of Jǔ made a covenant at Bāolái.
It is permissible to say "the Duke and the people,"
but it is not permissible to say "the Duke and a high official."
1.8.9 Locusts.
1.8.10 In winter,
in the twelfth month,
Wú Hāi died.
Wú Hāi's name
It has not been heard.
Someone said: Yǐn was not granted the rank of *dàfū*,
Someone said (therefore) he was demoted.
1.9 "Ninth Year of Duke Yǐn"
1.9.1 Ninth year,
spring,
The Heavenly King sent Nán Jì to come for an audience.
Nán,
is the family name,
Jì,
is the style name.
To have an audience,
is to inquire.
To have an audience with the feudal lords,
is not proper.
1.9.2 Third month,
*guǐ yǒu*,
heavy rain,
thunder, lightning.
Thunder,
is *léi*,
lightning,
is *tíng*.
1.9.3 *Gēng chén*,
heavy rain and snow,
To record is to be sparse.
Within eight days
there were further major changes,
yin and yang proceeded incorrectly,
therefore (it was) carefully recorded by day.
"Rain month"
means the record is correct.
1.9.4 Xiá died.
"Xiá" means,
what was "xiá-ed".
"Fú dàfū" means,
he was hidden (and) not granted the rank of dàfū.
Why was he hidden and not granted the rank of dàfū?
It is said,

When the five grains do not ripen, it is called a great famine.
If one grain does not ripen, it is called "qiàn" (嗛);

if three grains do not ripen, it is called "jǐn" (饉);
if four grains do not ripen, it is called "kāng" (康);
if five grains do not ripen, it is called "dà qīn" (大侵).
The rites for "dà qīn" (大侵) are:
the ruler does not eat dishes with multiple flavors,
platforms and pavilions are not plastered,
bows and arrows are relaxed (not used),
the roads in the court are not cleaned,
the officials are deployed but not controlled,

Gōngzǐ Jié (公子結) of Chǔ led an army to attack Chén (陳).
Wú (吳) came to the aid of Chén.
12.11 *Annals of Duke Āi*, Year 11
12.11.1 In the spring of the eleventh year,
Guó Shū (國書) of Qí (齊) led an army to attack us.
12.11.2 In summer,
Yuán Pō (轅頗) of Chén fled to Zhèng (鄭).
12.11.3 In the fifth month,
the Duke (公) met with Wú to attack Qí.
On the day of jiǎxū,
Guó Shū of Qí led an army and battled with Wú at Àilíng,
the Qí army was utterly defeated,
and Guó Shū of Qí was captured.
12.11.4 In the autumn, the seventh month, on the day of xīnyǒu,
the mother of the Viscount of Téng, Yú, died.
12.11.5 In the winter, the eleventh month,
Yǐngōng of Téng was buried.
12.11.6 Shìshū Qí of Wèi fled to Sòng.
12.12 *Āi Gōng* Year 12
12.12.1 In the spring of the twelfth year,
the *tián fù* land tax was implemented.
In ancient times, the public fields were taxed at one-tenth
On the day of jiǎxū,
. The use of the *tián fù* land tax
was not the proper way.
12.12.2 In the summer, the fifth month, on *jiǎ chén* day,
*Mèngzǐ* died.
Who was *Mèngzǐ*?
She was the wife of Duke *Zhāo*.
Why is she not referred to as "wife"?
It was to avoid mentioning that he married someone of the same surname.
12.12.3 The Duke met with *Wú* at *Tuógāo*.
12.12.4 In the autumn,
the Duke met with the Marquis of *Wèi* and
*Sòng Huáng Yuán* at *Yún*.
12.12.5 *Sòng Xiàng Cháo* led troops to attack *Zhèng*.
12.12.6 In the winter, the twelfth month,
locusts appeared.
12.13 *Āi Gōng* Year 13
12.13.1 In the spring of the thirteenth year,
Zhèng Hàn Dá led an army and seized soldiers of Sòng at Yán.
"Seized" and "exchanged" are words used to belittle.
To use an army and yet say "seized" rather than "exchanged"
Sòng was weakened.
12.13.2 In summer,
Xǔ Nán Chéng died.
12.13.3 The duke met with the Marquis of Jìn and the Viscount of Wú at Huáng Chí.
At the assembly of Huáng Chí,
did the Viscount of Wú advance?
He thereby became a viscount!
Wú was a state of the eastern barbarians,
cutting their hair short and tattooing their bodies.
Desiring to use the rituals of Lǔ,
and relying on the power of Jìn, he requested to wear the proper cap and ceremonial robes.
By relying on the Zhou court,
to honor the Heavenly King,
Wú advanced.
Wú, a great state of the east,
repeatedly brought small states to meet with the feudal lords,
to integrate with the Central States,
Wú was able to do this,
so how could he be considered a non-subject?
Wú advanced.
"King" is a term of respect;
"Zǐ" is a humble term.
Renouncing honorific titles and adopting a humble term
in order to meet with the various lords,
so as to honor the Heavenly King.
Wú Wáng Fūchāi said:
"A good cap is coming."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Great indeed is Fūchāi,
he cannot yet speak of a cap but desires to wear one."
12.13.4 Chǔ Gōngzǐ Shēn led an army to attack Chén.
12.13.5 Yuè invaded Wú.
12.13.6 In autumn,
the Duke returned from the assembly.
12.13.7 Jìn's Wèi Mànduō led an army to invade Wèi.
12.13.8 The burial of Xǔ Yuán Gōng.
12.13.9 In the ninth month, locusts appeared.
12.13.10 In the eleventh month of winter,
a comet appeared in the east.
12.13.11 Robbers killed Chén's Xià Qūfū.
12.13.12 In the twelfth month,
locusts.
12.14 *Āi Gōng* (哀公) Fourteenth Year
12.14.1 In the fourteenth year, spring,
(during the) western hunt, (they) captured a *lín* (麟, qilin).
This is to draw it in (to the records).
If the hunt is not in a hunting ground,
it is not considered a hunt.
It was not a hunt, yet it is called a hunt;
it was a great capture of a *lín*;
therefore, it greatly emphasizes its arrival.
The reason it does not say "came" (來),
is that it does not exclude the *lín* from the Central Kingdom (中國, Zhōngguó).
The reason it does not say "had" (有),
is to prevent the *lín* from not being a constant presence in the Central Kingdom.
